processing: As with other Chinese black teas, the leaf is withered, rolled, fully oxidised and dried. No fixed standard for this tea is widely documented.
harvest_season: Little is documented for this tea; Zhejiang black teas of this kind are usually made from spring leaf.
appearance_dry: Usually fine, dark twisted leaf, typical of new-style Zhejiang black teas.
appearance_liquor: A clear amber-orange, lighter than a robust Yunnan black.
appearance_wet: Soft, coppery brown small leaves, as is usual for tender-picked Chinese black tea.
taste_profile: Sold as a delicate black tea rather than a heavy one; expect a gentle, rounded cup with mild sweetness, as with other light new-style Chinese blacks.

brewing.notes: Typical handling for a delicate Chinese black: water a little off the boil and short steeps.

vintage_note: Little is documented about how this tea is sold. New-style Chinese black teas are usually offered by the year's spring harvest and are best drunk within a year or two.
description:
Anji Hong is a black tea from Anji county in northern Zhejiang, a place far better known for its pale green Anji Bai Cha. It is a newer, small-scale style, and shops describe it as delicate.

There is no well-documented recipe for it. It follows the general black tea path of withering, rolling, full oxidation and drying, which turns the leaf dark and the cup amber.

The cup is usually pitched as gentle, so treat it like other light Chinese blacks: water a little under boiling and short steeps. Long, hot steeps are the easy way to lose what makes a tea like this pleasant.

Ask the seller about harvest and maker, because the name is not a protected standard and one Anji Hong may differ a lot from another.
history: Little is documented about when Anji Hong first appeared. It is treated as a new style rather than an old regional tea, and Anji's tea reputation rests on its green tea.
sources_note: A snippet mentioned an Anji grower trying black tea from Bai Ye No. 1 leaf, but the exact page could not be attributed, so the claim is left out.
